title: Beef Pho
subtitle: Vietnamese clear beef noodle soup
excerpt: Vietnam's national dish: an extraordinarily aromatic, clear beef bone broth perfumed with charred ginger, star anise, cinnamon, and cloves, poured boiling over flat rice noodles and thin slices of raw beef that cook in the bowl.

recipe.sourceNotes: Pho (pronounced 'fuh') is the national soup of Vietnam, originating in the north of the country (Hanoi) in the early twentieth century, likely influenced by the French pot-au-feu and Chinese noodle soups during the colonial period. The dish spread south to Saigon, where it evolved to include a wider range of accompaniments (fresh bean sprouts, basil, lime). The broth is the heart of the dish and its preparation is the art: beef bones (ideally a mix of marrow bones and knuckles) are simmered for several hours, and the characteristic spiced aroma comes from charred onion and ginger combined with star anise, cinnamon, cloves, and coriander seeds. The broth must be very clear and very lightly coloured. The beef is sliced paper-thin and placed in the bowl; the boiling broth is poured over it to cook it to medium-rare. Pho is garnished with bean sprouts, fresh herbs, lime, and chilli.

content.text: Blanch the bones first (cover with cold water, bring to the boil, drain and rinse) to remove impurities that would cloud the broth. Char the onion and ginger directly over the gas flame or under the grill until blackened in spots; this gives the broth its characteristic colour and sweetness. The broth must be kept at a barely visible simmer; boiling makes it cloudy.

content.text: Cover the brisket with cold water, bring to the boil, drain, and rinse. Return to the pot with 3 litres of fresh cold water. Add the charred onion, charred ginger, star anise, cinnamon, cloves, and coriander seeds. Bring to a very gentle simmer. Skim carefully. Simmer for 3 hours.
Remove the brisket. Strain the broth through a fine sieve. Season with fish sauce, sugar, and salt. The broth should be clear, amber-coloured, deeply aromatic, and lightly saline.

Cook the soaked noodles in boiling water for 2 minutes. Drain. Divide the noodles between deep bowls. Arrange the raw sirloin slices over the noodles. Bring the broth to a rolling boil. Pour it directly over the raw beef in the bowls; the boiling broth will cook it to medium-rare. Top with spring onion, coriander, bean sprouts, chilli, and lime.
